correctness.rationale: For any Fano point pair carrying the same two-name label, the line through them must carry the complementary label. The remaining four points form a four-cycle under lines through the repeated points and two diagonal pairs under the third point. Each of the four names must occur at least twice on those four points, saturating all eight occurrences; the two complementary-name supports are the distinct diagonals, so only eight completions exist. The repeated label is unique; counting 21 point pairs, six pair labels and eight completions yields 1008. Point and line classes of the Heawood incidence graph independently satisfy dual Fano conditions, giving 1008^2. All six pair labels occur, so the four sets are distinct and S4 acts freely; unlabelled count is 1008^2/24. The GL(3,2) pair stabilizer has order eight and acts freely/transitively on the eight completions. The checker independently enumerated all 6^7 assignments and verified the action with 168 collineations.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical cubic graph with total domatic number one and the Fano incidence graph used as the exceptional construction in the October 2026 all-cubic existence proof. The exact number of four-set witnesses is a natural question about abundance beyond existence. The result gives a complete geometric classification (one repeated pair label and eight canonical completions), a one-orbit rigidity theorem and named/unlabelled counts for the whole graph. This is a meaningful exact classification at the central exceptional example rather than an arbitrary finite slice; claims are explicitly limited to that graph.
